cases.name: dev-crop-type-sentinel2
cases.promptMarkdown: I'm doing a master's project on crop type classification from Sentinel-2 image time series. I need ground-truth labels for actual crops (wheat, maize, rapeseed and so on, not just cropland versus non-cropland) for individual fields or pixels, already paired with multi-temporal Sentinel-2 data, because I don't have time to build my own download and preprocessing pipeline. The data also needs a licence that lets me publish results and share trained models. Which benchmark datasets fit, and where do I get them?

graders.name: 01-recall-breizhcrops
graders.evidence:
## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** labels for specific crop types (wheat, maize, rapeseed and so on) per field or pixel.
- **R2 (must):** ready-made multi-temporal Sentinel-2 data already paired with those labels, so you don't build a pipeline.
- **R3 (must):** a licence that lets you publish results and share trained models.
- I assumed you want something you can download now, not something behind an application.

## Shortlist
Every dataset here is a direct download with no account or application. The registry record confirmed the licence on 2026-11-11, except where the table says otherwise.

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PASTIS (France, parcel patches) | Direct download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | 28.8 GB | Strong | Today |
| 2 | EuroCropsML (Europe, per-parcel series) | Direct download, minutes | CC-BY-SA-4.0 | Not recorded | Strong | Today |
| 3 | BreizhCrops (Brittany, about 600k parcels) | Direct download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | Not recorded | Strong | Partly: the registry lookup failed, so the licence comes from the search record |
| 4 | TimeSen2Crop (Austria, 16 crops, pixels) | Direct download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | about 1 GB | Strong | Today |
| 5 | AgriSen-COG (AT, BE, ES, DK, NL) | Direct download; check which parts are on Zenodo | CC-BY-4.0 | Large | Strong | Today (label part) |
| 6 | Sen4AgriNet, TACO repackaging (Catalonia and France) | Direct download from Hugging Face | CC-BY-SA-4.0 | 10,013 patches | Strong | Today |
| 7 | CropHarvest (global) | Direct download, minutes | CC-BY-SA-4.0 | Not recorded | Partial | Today |
| 8 | Brandenburg-S12-CropVal | Direct download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | Not recorded | Partial | Today |
| 9 | Peru multi-annual S2 crop dataset (2026) | Direct download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | Not recorded | Partial | Today |
| 10 | IBM/NASA multi-temporal crop classification (US) | Direct download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | Not recorded | Partial | Today |

## Details

**1. PASTIS** (https://zenodo.org/records/5012942)
- It has parcel-level Sentinel-2 time series patches for France, with crop-type semantic and instance labels. It's the most used benchmark of this kind, with about 93k Zenodo downloads.
- From memory, not confirmed: it has 18 crop classes, and a companion repository holds the code and splits.
- Download the 28.8 GB zip from the record page.
- It is in patch (segmentation) format rather than pixel tables, so you may need to convert it for pixel-wise or parcel-wise models.

**2. EuroCropsML** (https://zenodo.org/records/15095445)
- Per-parcel median Sentinel-2 L1C time series with 176 crop classes and 706,683 labelled points. Both figures come from the paper abstract. It was built for few-shot transfer across countries.
- It is CC-BY-SA, so derivatives must stay share-alike. Whether a trained model counts as a derivative is legally unsettled, so ask your supervisor or library.
- The data are per-parcel medians, so there is no spatial context.
- Papers that used it:
  - The dataset paper: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-04952-7
  - A 2026 baselines paper: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ophoto.2026.100117

**3. BreizhCrops** (https://zenodo.org/records/14585341)
- Parcels in Brittany with both top-of-atmosphere and bottom-of-atmosphere Sentinel-2 series. The paper abstract says reference models, pretrained weights and a GitHub repository (dl4sits/breizhcrops) come with it.
- From memory: one region and one year (2017).
- The dataset paper compares seven deep networks and a random forest baseline, so you get ready comparisons: https://doi.org/10.5194/isprs-archives-xliii-b2-2020-1545-2020

**4. TimeSen2Crop** (https://zenodo.org/records/4715631)
- More than 1 million pixel samples for 16 crop types, September 2017 to August 2018. Atmospherically corrected, with cloud, snow and shadow flags.
- The download is about 1 GB, and it has about 2.8k Zenodo downloads. This is the easiest one to start with.
- From memory: the area is Austria.
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1109/jstars.2021.3073965

**5. AgriSen-COG** (https://zenodo.org/records/7892012)
- It has Sentinel-2 cloud-optimised GeoTIFFs for five countries, labelled from farmer declarations (LPIS).
- The Zenodo record I verified holds the label part. Check the paper for where the imagery lives.
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.3390/rs15122980

**6. Sen4AgriNet, TACO repackaging** (https://huggingface.co/datasets/isp-uv-es/sen4agrinet-taco)
- It has 10,013 Sentinel-2 patches over Catalonia and France for 2019–2020, with 168 harmonised crop and land-cover classes.
- This is a third-party repackaging with a split the repackager constructed, not the original authors' release. The card says to follow the original licence, and I haven't checked that one.
- Original paper: https://doi.org/10.1109/jstars.2022.3164771

**7. CropHarvest** (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10251170)
- Global labels with time series. From memory, most labels are crop versus non-crop, with a multiclass subset. Check how many specific-crop labels you get before committing.

**8–10. Brandenburg-S12-CropVal, Peru, IBM/NASA**
- Brandenburg-S12-CropVal (https://zenodo.org/records/18632974):
  - It is a Sentinel-1/2 cropland segmentation set for cross-regional transfer.
  - I haven't read its class list, so I don't know whether the labels are specific crops.
- Peru (https://zenodo.org/records/19949051):
  - Multi-annual Sentinel-2 crop type data, new in 2026, with no papers using it yet.
  - I haven't read its class list.
- IBM/NASA (https://huggingface.co/datasets/ibm-nasa-geospatial/multi-temporal-crop-classification):
  - This is a US dataset built from HLS imagery, which is a 30 m Landsat–Sentinel-2 composite, not native 10 m Sentinel-2.
  - From memory, it has 13 classes.

**On licences (R3).** All the licences above allow publishing results. Plain CC-BY (PASTIS, BreizhCrops, TimeSen2Crop, AgriSen-COG, and the Brandenburg, Peru and IBM/NASA sets) is the safest for sharing trained models. The CC-BY-SA datasets (EuroCropsML, Sen4AgriNet, CropHarvest) are fine for results. For released models, check how your university treats share-alike. If you want no ambiguity, start with 1, 3 or 4.

## Known, not confirmed
- **ZueriCrop:** the Hugging Face copy (https://huggingface.co/datasets/isaaccorley/zuericrop) is CC-BY-NC-4.0. I didn't check the original release or licence. A non-commercial licence may complicate sharing models.
- **Original Sen4AgriNet release (GitHub):** I didn't check its home page or licence.
- **S2Agri / PixelSet:** Hugging Face copies exist under monster-monash (CC-BY-4.0), but I didn't check the original home or access terms.
- **DENETHOR (Germany):** I searched for it but didn't confirm a record, so I can't say where it lives now.

## Not recommended, and why
- **EuroCrops:** parcel labels only, with no imagery. EuroCropsML is the version paired with Sentinel-2.
- **CropNet:** county-level yield prediction, not field or pixel crop type.
- **Hugging Face ZueriCrop copy:** non-commercial licence, as noted above.

## What I could not find
- Zenodo and DataCite failed intermittently during the search, so coverage may be incomplete.
- I didn't confirm the sizes of several entries, and I didn't get class lists for the three partial-fit datasets.
- Everything marked "from memory" above was not confirmed today.

## Next step
Download TimeSen2Crop (about 1 GB) and BreizhCrops first and get a baseline running. Then add PASTIS or EuroCropsML if you want spatial context or cross-country transfer. Before you commit to a dataset, open the dataset page or paper to confirm the class list and licence, because these were checked on 2026-11-11 and can change.

The interactive page is at `/private/tmp/e-W4YHCE/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

graders.name: 01-recall-breizhcrops
graders.evidence:
These are the benchmarks I'd shortlist. I'm working from memory and haven't checked the licence pages live, so confirm each licence on the dataset's own page before you publish.

## Best fits (field or parcel-level, Sentinel-2 time series included)

| Dataset | Region / labels | What you get | Licence (as I recall) | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PASTIS / PASTIS-R** | France, 18 crop classes plus background, ~2,400 parcel-annotated patches | Sentinel-2 time series (PASTIS-R adds Sentinel-1). Parcel-level semantic and panoptic labels. A standard benchmark, so you can compare against published results. | CC-BY 4.0 | Zenodo ("PASTIS"), code at `VSainteuf/pastis-benchmark` on GitHub |
| **BreizhCrops** | Brittany, France, ~600k field-level time series, 9 main crop classes | Sentinel-2 L1C and L2A pixel-aggregated per field. It has a PyTorch loader and is easy to use for per-field sequence models (LSTM, Transformer, TempCNN). | CC-BY 4.0 (code MIT) | `dl4sits/BreizhCrops` on GitHub, Zenodo |
| **Sen4AgriNet** | Catalonia and France, multi-year, hierarchical labels (many classes) | Sentinel-2 time series with parcel labels from CAP declarations. It is large, so a good fit if you want scale. | CC-BY 4.0 | GitHub (`Orion-AI-Lab/S4A`) |
| **CropHarvest** | Global, point-level labels, a multi-class subset for crop types | Pre-extracted Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, ERA5 and SRTM time series per point. It has good coverage outside Europe, but labels are sparse and uneven by region. | Mostly CC-BY-SA 4.0 (varies by sub-dataset) | Zenodo, `nasaharvest/cropharvest` on GitHub |
| **ZueriCrop** | Zurich and Thurgau, Switzerland, ~48 classes | Sentinel-2 time series with instance-level field labels. | Check the repo | `0zgur0/ms-convSTAR` on GitHub |
| **Radiant MLHub / Source Cooperative crop-type sets** | South Africa (Western Cape), Kenya, Ghana, Tanzania and others | Smallholder-region field labels paired with Sentinel-2 (and sometimes Sentinel-1). Radiant MLHub was migrated to Source Cooperative in 2024, so look there. | Mostly CC-BY 4.0, per dataset | source.coop |

## Also worth knowing
- **EuroCrops** has harmonised EU LPIS crop labels with a common taxonomy (HCAT). It is labels only, with no Sentinel-2 attached, so you'd have to build the pairing yourself. Skip it given your time constraint, unless you need many countries. The licence is CC-BY-SA 4.0.
- **Munich480** (Bavaria) and **TimeMatch** (several regions, aimed at domain adaptation) are Sentinel-2 crop-type sets. Check their licences before relying on them.
- **GEO-Bench and PANGAEA** bundle several crop-type tasks, including PASTIS-R and a South Africa crop-type set. They give you ready-made splits and baselines, which helps if you want a comparison table.

## Recommendation
- **Start with PASTIS-R.** It is parcel-level, covers many crop types and has permissive licensing. It has the most published baselines, so your results will be comparable.
- **Add BreizhCrops** if you want a lightweight per-field time-series task, or if you want a second dataset to show your model generalises.
- **Add CropHarvest or a Source Cooperative set** if you want a non-European test region.

## Licence points to check
- **CC-BY** (PASTIS, BreizhCrops, Sen4AgriNet) only needs attribution. It allows publishing results and sharing trained models.
- **CC-BY-SA** (CropHarvest, EuroCrops) is also fine for publishing results. The share-alike clause applies clearly to redistributed or derived datasets. Whether it reaches trained model weights is legally unsettled, so read the terms or ask your supervisor if you plan to release weights.
- Many of these labels come from government LPIS or CAP data under open-government licences, and the Sentinel-2 imagery is free and open under Copernicus terms. Cite the original data providers as well as the benchmark paper.

I can fetch the current licence text and download links for any of these if you want. I'd need to use web access for that.

graders.name: 01-recall-low-carbon-london
graders.evidence:
Yes, you can start today. The best-fitting datasets (GoiEner, London, Norwegian iFlex, Swiss HEAPO) are open downloads. The Irish CER trial needs a signed form, and the large UK SERL data needs months of accreditation.

I checked these on 2026-11-12 against Zenodo, the London Datastore, data.gov.au and the Pecan Street site. Three official pages (ISSDA, SERL, Ausgrid's own) blocked or failed my tool, so those access details come from web-search summaries and memory.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** per-household smart-meter series, hundreds of households or more.
- **R2 (must):** at least a year of history per household.
- **R3 (must):** hourly or finer resolution.
- I assumed non-commercial research use, and that you'd rather start now than wait months.

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [GoiEner](https://zenodo.org/records/7362094) (Spain) | Open download, minutes | CC BY (inconsistent, see below) | 25,559 raw series, hourly, 2014–2022 | Strong | Today |
| 2 | [Low Carbon London](https://data.london.gov.uk/dataset/smartmeter-energy-consumption-data-in-london-households-vqm0d) | Open download, minutes | Not stated in what I read | 5,567 households, half-hourly, 2011–14 | Strong | Today |
| 3 | [iFlex](https://zenodo.org/records/8248802) (Norway) | Open download, minutes | CC BY 4.0 | Hourly, 2020–21 | Partial | Today |
| 4 | [HEAPO](https://zenodo.org/records/15056919) (Switzerland) | Open download, minutes | CC BY 4.0 | 1,408 homes, 15-min, 2018–24 | Partial | Today |
| 5 | [Irish CER trial](https://www.ucd.ie/issda/data/commissionforenergyregulationcer/) | Signed request form, days | ISSDA terms | >5,000 homes and businesses, half-hourly | Strong | Web search and memory |
| 6 | [SERL Observatory](https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/8666) (UK) | Accredited-researcher application, months | UKDS secure agreement | ~13k homes, half-hourly, 2019–24 | Strong | Web search |
| 7 | [Smart-Grid Smart-City](https://data.gov.au/data/dataset/smart-grid-smart-city-customer-trial-data) (Australia) | Open download, minutes | CC BY 4.0 | Half-hourly, 2010–14 | Partial | Today |
| 8 | [Ausgrid Solar Home](https://data.gov.au/data/dataset/nsw-solar-home-electricty-data) | Open, but see caveat | Not checked | 300 homes, half-hourly, 3 years | Partial | Today |
| 9 | [Pecan Street Dataport](https://www.pecanstreet.org/dataport/) (US) | Free academic account, days | Non-commercial only | 75 homes in the free tier, 1-min | Partial | Today |

## Details
**GoiEner** (start here for scale)
- Hourly kWh for a Spanish energy cooperative's customers, 2014-11 to 2022-06.
- It comes as raw (2 GB) and imputed files (about 0.5–0.8 GB each), plus a metadata file. The imputed files only include series longer than a year, which covers your R2.
- It includes some small businesses, farms and industrial tariffs. Filter on the tariff column (2.X is households and small businesses).
- The Zenodo page says CC-BY-SA in the description but CC BY 4.0 in the rights field. Cite the WHY project.
- The 2020–21 pandemic period is in the data.

**Low Carbon London**
- This is the most-used UK benchmark: a representative sample, about 167 million rows and 10 GB unzipped.
- About 1,100 households were on dynamic time-of-use prices in 2013, with the price given a day ahead. Treat them as a confound for day-ahead forecasting, or exclude them.
- Many households have less than the full 2.3 years.
- A published day-ahead benchmark used 71 filtered households from it: [Benchmarking of Load Forecasting Methods Using Residential Smart Meter Data](https://doi.org/10.3390/app12199844) (2022).

**Irish CER trial**
- Download the Research Purposes request form from the ISSDA page, sign it and email it to issda@ucd.ie.
- It runs about 1.5 years (from memory) and mixes homes and businesses, so you'll need to filter to residential.
- Don't use unofficial mirrors. A ScienceDB copy turned up in the registry, and I didn't verify its permissions.

**SERL**
- You need Accredited Researcher status through the ONS accreditation service (every team member), the UKDS Secure Access agreement and approval from the SERL governance board.
- You can't download the data, and you must be in the UK when you access it.
- SERL's site quotes 4–6 weeks for review. The UKDS guidance says 3–4 months overall.
- There is also a [safeguarded SERL statistical dataset](https://doi.org/10.5255/ukda-sn-8963-1), but it is aggregated, so it doesn't meet your per-household requirement.

**Pecan Street**
- The free tier covers 75 homes (25 each in Austin, New York and California) for non-commercial academic use.
- Paid university tiers start at $10,000. That is too small for "hundreds of households" unless you pay.

## Known, not confirmed
- **Smart-Grid Smart-City:** the page confirms half-hourly data for the trial, but I haven't checked per-customer history. I recall about 13,000 customers, and many have partial coverage.
- **Ausgrid Solar Home:** all 300 homes have rooftop PV, so consumption and generation are separate channels. One user's quality screening kept only about 54 homes. Ausgrid's own page returned 404 to my tool. Check whether the data.gov.au link still serves the files.
- **iFlex:** it spans about two winters (early 2020 to spring 2021), so many households may have under a year. Check the lengths.

## Not recommended, and why
- **Electricity Load Diagrams (UCI, 370 clients):** Portuguese clients that are mostly commercial or industrial, not homes. It is a common forecasting benchmark, so it's easy to mistake for household data.
- **UK-DALE, REFIT, ECO:** these are household datasets, but they have only about 5 to 20 homes each (from memory).
- **Synthetic sets (ResStock-based, LPG-derived, OpenSynth):** simulated rather than measured.

## What I could not find
- I did not check per-household history length inside any dataset. For R2, count households with at least 365 days after you download.
- I found no other open household set at this scale with 1+ years of hourly data. The registry search also returned many small or country-specific sets that I did not review individually.

## Next step
Download GoiEner (filtered to household tariffs) and Low Carbon London (excluding the time-of-use group) now, and send the ISSDA form in parallel since it takes days. Only start the SERL accreditation if you need UK data from after 2014, because it takes months.

Interactive shortlist: `/private/tmp/e-N4S1wE/home/cwd/dataset-scout/dataset-shortlist.html`

- **London:** the [London Datastore page](https://data.london.gov.uk/dataset/smartmeter-energy-consumption-data-in-london-households-vqm0d) offers a zip of about 765 MB. Households join and leave at different times, so filter for those with a full year. This is the most-used household benchmark, and one day-ahead study on it is [Benchmarking of Load Forecasting Methods Using Residential Smart Meter Data](https://doi.org/10.3390/app12199844). Use this official copy rather than the Kaggle or GitHub mirrors.
- **ECD-UY:** by far the largest. The [figshare record](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.16965400) is CC0, and its paper is [Sci. Data 2022](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-022-01122-x). It is a southern-hemisphere climate with little weather metadata.
- **Swiss:** the [Zenodo record](https://zenodo.org/records/21398769) was published in July 2026. It covers apartments and houses, including homes with heat pumps, EVs and PV. It has two full years but few published baselines yet.
- **HEAPO:** the [Zenodo record](https://zenodo.org/records/15056919) has the longest history, but every home has a heat pump, so demand is strongly weather-driven and unrepresentative.
- **iFlex:** the [Zenodo record](https://zenodo.org/records/8248802) includes surveys. It comes from a price-response experiment during COVID, which distorts day-ahead patterns, and it spans only about a year. Check Table 1 of its paper for exact counts.
- **Smart-Grid Smart-City:** the [data.gov.au page](https://data.gov.au/data/dataset/smart-grid-smart-city-customer-trial-data) has half-hourly readings per household. The trial's tariffs and in-home displays may affect behaviour.

For your benchmark, I'd start with GoiEner, London and ECD-UY. They cover three different countries and climates.

## Known, not confirmed

- **Irish CER Smart Metering Trial (ISSDA, UCD):** about 5,000 homes and businesses at 30 min over 2009–2010, about 1.5 years. It is widely used in the literature.
  - **Access:** the search results (not the page) say you complete and sign a request form and email it to ISSDA. That is an application rather than a download. Time to access is unknown, probably days to weeks.
  - **What I tried:** the ISSDA site refused automated requests (HTTP 403), so I couldn't read the terms.
  - **What to check:** the [ISSDA dataset page](https://www.ucd.ie/issda/data/commissionforenergyregulationcer/) for the form and terms.

## Not recommended, and why

- **Pecan Street Dataport:** the free academic tier covers only 75 homes. More needs a paid licence (from web search).
- **Ausgrid Solar Home data:** 300 solar homes at 30 min over 3 years. It is small and PV-skewed, and a repo note says it may have been removed from Ausgrid's site. Public copies exist on [data.gov.au](https://www.data.gov.au/data/en/dataset/nsw-solar-home-electricty-data).
- **IDEAL Household Energy Dataset:** I recall roughly 255 homes, from memory and not confirmed. That is small for your threshold.
- **Kaggle, Hugging Face and Zenodo re-uploads of the London data:** these are third-party copies. Use the official source.

## What I could not find

- I did not check the documentation of every dataset for the share of households with a complete year. Do this yourself for London, iFlex and SGSC.
- Registry searches on DataCite and Hugging Face sometimes returned malformed responses, so the list may be incomplete. I searched Zenodo, OpenAIRE, DataCite, Hugging Face and PhysioNet, plus the web.
- The London and SGSC access and licence details come from a web search summary, not the registry record.

## Next step

Download GoiEner and London first and build your day-ahead baseline on them. Then validate on ECD-UY. If you want an Irish comparison, send the ISSDA request now, since it's the only one with a wait.

The interactive page is at `/private/tmp/e-qVHPie/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`. I didn't commit anything.

graders.name: 01-recall-low-carbon-london
graders.evidence:
I'm answering from memory and didn't check the current links or licenses, so confirm those on each landing page. Here are the datasets that fit your criteria (individual households, hundreds or more, at least a year, hourly or finer):

| Dataset | Households | Resolution | Span | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **GoiEner** (Basque Country, Spain) | about 25,000 | hourly | several years | **Direct download** from Zenodo (CC-BY). It's the largest open option and has metadata such as tariff and postcode. |
| **London Smart Meters** (UK Power Networks, Low Carbon London) | about 5,500 | 30 min | Nov 2011 to Feb 2014 | **Direct download** from the London Datastore and Kaggle. About 1,100 households were on a dynamic time-of-use tariff, which you'd need to handle. Many households have gaps or start late. |
| **Ausgrid Solar Home** (Sydney) | 300 | 30 min | 3 years | **Direct download** from Ausgrid's site. All homes have rooftop PV, so net and gross load differ, which matters for forecasting. |
| **Smart Grid Smart City** (Australia) | tens of thousands | 30 min | about 2012 to 2014 | **Direct download** from data.gov.au. The data is messy, and coverage varies by customer. |
| **CER Irish Smart Metering Trial** | about 4,000 homes (plus about 1,000 SMEs) | 30 min | about 1.5 years (2009 to 2010) | **Application required** through ISSDA. It's free for research, but you sign a data-use agreement, and approval can take days. |
| **Pecan Street Dataport** (US) | hundreds to thousands | 1 min to 15 min, including circuit-level | varies by home | **Application required**. Academic access is free, and commercial use is paid. A small sample is open. |

**Practical notes**
- **Fastest start:** GoiEner is the best match for your criteria and needs no application. London is the most widely used benchmark, so it gives you the most published results to compare against. The CER data is a common benchmark but requires an application.
- **Datasets that look like matches but aren't:**
  - The UCI *ElectricityLoadDiagrams* data (370 clients, Portugal) is mostly commercial and industrial customers, not homes.
  - REFIT, UK-DALE and Smart* have only about 5 to 20 homes each.
  - ResStock and Buildings-900K are simulated, not measured.
- **Weather and calendar features:** none of these ship with weather data. You'll need to join it yourself, for example from ERA5, Met Office or Bureau of Meteorology data. Day-ahead benchmarks usually need temperature and holiday calendars.
- **Representativeness:** the datasets cover different countries, years and tariffs, and Ausgrid is PV-only. Using two or three of them would make your benchmark more robust.

I can check the current download links and licenses, or write a loader that puts these into one common schema.

graders.name: 01-recall-physionet-2019-sepsis-challenge
graders.evidence:
## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** adult ICU time series of routine vitals and labs.
- **R2 (must):** a time-stamped sepsis onset label (Sepsis-3 or close), or data you can derive one from.
- **R3 (must):** thousands of patients in a clear setting.
- **R4 (nice to have):** data you can get within about a week.

I checked everything against PhysioNet's registry and pages on 2026-11-11/12. I marked anything I didn't re-read today as "memory".

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2019, sepsis | **Open download, minutes** | CC-BY-4.0 | 40,336 ICU stays | Strong; label included | Today |
| 2 | MIMIC-IV v3.1 | Credentialed, days to weeks | PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License | Large (single centre) | Strong; you derive the label | Today |
| 3 | eICU-CRD v2.0 | Credentialed, same route as MIMIC-IV | PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License | Multi-centre US | Strong; you derive the label | Today |
| 4 | HiRID v1.1.1 | Credentialed plus author approval, weeks | PhysioNet Contributor Review Health Data License | ~34k admissions | Strong; you derive the label | Today |
| 5 | SICdb v1.0.8 | Credentialed plus contributor approval, weeks | PhysioNet Contributor Review Health Data License | Not checked | Partial; label unclear | Today |
| 6 | AmsterdamUMCdb | Application, DANS licence | DANS Licence | ~23k admissions (memory) | Strong if the Sepsis-3 code works | Registry record only; access terms from memory |

## Details
**1. Challenge 2019 (start here).** Link: https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2019/1.0.0/
- It has hourly vitals and labs plus an hourly sepsis label, so you can run a baseline this week.
- The label is a challenge convention, not a charted event. From memory, onset is set 6 hours before clinical suspicion of infection, using Sepsis-3 criteria.
- It has only about 40 variables, with shifted times. You can't re-derive onset from source tables, and the hidden test set was never released.
- Don't use the Hugging Face copies. They are unofficial.

**2–5. PhysioNet credentialed datasets.** All four share one route:
1. Create a PhysioNet account.
2. Complete the CITI "Data or Specimens Only Research" course. Per PhysioNet's instructions, affiliate with "Massachusetts Institute of Technology Affiliates" and upload the training report, not the certificate.
3. Submit the credentialing application.
4. Sign the data use agreement for each dataset.

- PhysioNet's registry text says only credentialed users who sign the agreement can access the files.
- Access is personal, so each person on your team applies separately.
- One credentialing covers all of these datasets, but each needs its own agreement.
- HiRID and SICdb add a step. You submit a specific research question and the authors or contributors approve it. The pages say this, so budget extra time for it.
- None of these has a Sepsis-3 column. You derive onset from SOFA plus suspected infection (antibiotic and culture timing). MIMIC-IV is the easiest for this, because it has well-documented antibiotic and culture tables and open community code (from memory).
- eICU has a demo (100 stays, open, ODbL licence) at https://physionet.org/content/eicu-crd-demo/2.0.1/. MIMIC-IV has one too at https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-demo/2.2/. You can build your pipeline on these while you wait.
- Don't paste restricted records into hosted AI tools. PhysioNet's 24 Sept 2025 policy prohibits it unless zero retention and no training are verified.

**6. AmsterdamUMCdb.** Link: https://doi.org/10.17026/dans-22u-f8vd
- The registry lists it as application-based under the DANS Licence.
- A GigaDB record titled "Sepsis-3 criteria in AmsterdamUMCdb: open-source code implementation" exists (https://doi.org/10.5524/102204).
- The landing and access pages wouldn't load, so the process is from memory: a request plus a signed licence agreement. Confirm it before planning around it.

## Known, not confirmed
- **AmsterdamUMCdb access steps and timing.** I know the registry says "application". I tried the DOI, the DataCite API and GitHub, and all failed with connection errors. Check the DOI page.
- **SICdb sepsis fit.** The page lists sepsis detection as an application area. I didn't verify antibiotic or culture data, which you'd need to derive onset. Check https://www.sicdb.com/Documentation/.
- **Challenge 2019 label definition.** The 6-hour rule is from memory. Check it against the challenge paper.

## Not recommended, and why
- **PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2012.** It predicts mortality only.
- **GOSSIS-1 / WiDS 2020.** These are severity-score summaries, not time series with onset.
- **Zigong infection ICU database.** It is a single-hospital infection cohort. I didn't check it for onset labels or time series, and it needs credentialing.
- **Zenodo sepsis records.** These are small clinical-study supplements or unrelated records, not ICU time series.

## What I could not find
- **Literature evidence of use.** The paper search returned almost nothing, so I have no verified papers to cite for any dataset. Search for the 2019 challenge's official results paper and for HiRID benchmark papers yourself.
- **Newer derived datasets.** I saw MIMIC-IV-Ext-CLIF in the results but didn't evaluate it. I also didn't look for pre-built Sepsis-3 tables.

## Next step
1. Today, download Challenge 2019 and build the baseline.
2. Today, start the CITI course and the PhysioNet credentialing application. Ask your supervisor for the reference or sign-off the form needs.
3. In parallel, develop your Sepsis-3 derivation on the MIMIC-IV demo, then run it on full MIMIC-IV once approved.
4. Use eICU or HiRID later for external validation.

I can't say how long credentialing will take from this check. Confirm the current review times on PhysioNet.

Interactive page: `/private/tmp/e-HIuBPH/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |

| 2 | MIMIC-IV v3.1 | Credentialed: CITI training and DUA, about 1–2 weeks | PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License | tens of thousands of ICU stays | Strong (derive onset) | access today, contents from memory |
| 3 | eICU-CRD | Credentialed, same application as MIMIC-IV | PhysioNet Credentialed | about 200k stays | Strong (derive onset) | access today, contents from memory |
| 4 | HiRID (Bern) | Credentialed plus authors' approval of your research question, weeks | PhysioNet Contributor Review | about 34k admissions | Strong (derive onset) | today |
| 5 | AmsterdamUMCdb v1.0.2 | Signed access and licence form via DANS, weeks | DANS Licence | tens of thousands of admissions | Strong (derive onset) | access today |
| 6 | SICdb (Salzburg) | Credentialed plus contributor approval, weeks | PhysioNet Contributor Review | not checked | Partial | today |
| 7 | MIMIC-IV demo / eICU demo | Open, minutes | ODbL-1.0 | about 100 / about 2,500 stays (from memory) | Pipeline testing only | today |

## Details

**1. Challenge 2019: start here today.**
- Link: https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2019/
- The page states there is one hourly file per subject. It has two hospital systems (sets A and B, 20,336 and 20,000 subjects).
- Labels come from Sepsis-3, and the page says they are "shifted… ahead by six hours", so the task is already 6-hour-early prediction.
- Download needs no credentials.
- Caveats:
  - It has a fixed set of about 40 variables, from memory.
  - You can't re-derive the label.
  - The challenge's hidden test set isn't included.
- Official scoring code and a utility function that rewards early predictions are provided.

**2–3. MIMIC-IV and eICU: the main research data.**
- Links: https://physionet.org/content/mimiciv/ and https://physionet.org/content/eicu-crd/
- Neither has an onset column. You derive Sepsis-3 from SOFA plus suspected infection (antibiotics and cultures). Community derivation code exists, from memory.
- Access steps, confirmed on the pages:
  1. Create a PhysioNet account.
  2. Complete CITI's "Data or Specimens Only Research" course. PhysioNet says to affiliate with "Massachusetts Institute of Technology Affiliates" and not register as an independent learner, which avoids extra fees.
  3. Upload the CITI training report, not the certificate.
  4. Apply for credentialing. A reference may be requested, from memory.
  5. Sign the data use agreement.
- Access is personal, so your supervisor and lab mates each apply separately.
- Don't send this data to hosted LLM services. PhysioNet's rule is at https://physionet.org/news/post/llm-responsible-use/.
- MIMIC-IV is single-centre. eICU is multi-centre and is the natural external-validation set.

**4. HiRID.**
- Link: https://physionet.org/content/hirid/
- It has roughly 2-minute resolution from a Swiss ICU, which suits time-series modelling.
- The page says you must be credentialed, sign the DUA "and provide a specific research question". The data authors approve the request, so timing is less predictable.

**5. AmsterdamUMCdb.**
- Link: https://doi.org/10.17026/dans-22u-f8vd
- The record is restricted and points to a signed access request and end-use licence form (details at github.com/AmsterdamUMC/AmsterdamUMCdb). Whether the form needs an institutional signature is from memory, so check it.
- A DataCite record titled "Sepsis-3 criteria in AmsterdamUMCdb: open-source code implementation" exists, which could save you derivation work.

**6. SICdb.** The page says contributor approval is required, along with PhysioNet credentialing and a research question. It is a possible later validation site.

**7. Demos.** The open MIMIC-IV and eICU samples are too small to model. Use them to write and test your Sepsis-3 pipeline while credentialing is pending.

## Known, not confirmed

- **Paper citations:** the literature APIs returned almost nothing, so I'm citing no papers. Check the Challenge 2019 paper (Reyna et al., *Critical Care Medicine*), which the page says is the official one.
- **Contents of MIMIC-IV, eICU and AmsterdamUMCdb:** I didn't read the variable lists today. Sizes and derivation code availability are from memory.
- **Credentialing timing:** "about 1–2 weeks" is from memory.

## Not recommended, and why

- **Hugging Face copies of the Challenge data:** unofficial mirrors. Use PhysioNet.
- **Zenodo and OpenAIRE sepsis supplements:** these have mortality, biomarker or single-study tables, with no hourly vitals or onset times.
- **MIMIC-style datasets with only discharge codes:** ICD-coded sepsis gives no onset time.

## What I could not find

- An open, multi-centre dataset with raw Sepsis-3 inputs and no application.
- Working literature search results this session.
- The old Amsterdam URL (amsterdammedicaldatascience.nl/amsterdamumcdb/) returned 404, so use the DOI link.

## Next step

1. Today: download Challenge 2019 and run a baseline against its utility score.
2. Today: start the CITI course and the PhysioNet credentialing application. That is the slow part.
3. While you wait: build your Sepsis-3 derivation on the MIMIC-IV demo.
4. After approval: train on MIMIC-IV and validate externally on eICU. Ask the HiRID authors in parallel.

- Neither has an onset column. You derive Sepsis-3 from SOFA plus suspected infection (antibiotics and cultures). Community derivation code exists, from memory.
- Access steps, confirmed on the pages:
  1. Create a PhysioNet account.
  2. Complete CITI's "Data or Specimens Only Research" course. PhysioNet says to affiliate with "Massachusetts Institute of Technology Affiliates" and not register as an independent learner, which avoids extra fees.
  3. Upload the CITI training report, not the certificate.
  4. Apply for credentialing. A reference may be requested, from memory.
  5. Sign the data use agreement.
- Access is personal, so your supervisor and lab mates each apply separately.
- Don't send this data to hosted LLM services. PhysioNet's rule is at https://physionet.org/news/post/llm-responsible-use/.
- MIMIC-IV is single-centre. eICU is multi-centre and is the natural external-validation set.

- Link: https://physionet.org/content/hirid/
- It has roughly 2-minute resolution from a Swiss ICU, which suits time-series modelling.
- The page says you must be credentialed, sign the DUA "and provide a specific research question". The data authors approve the request, so timing is less predictable.

**5. AmsterdamUMCdb.**
- Link: https://doi.org/10.17026/dans-22u-f8vd

**6. SICdb.** The page says contributor approval is required, along with PhysioNet credentialing and a research question. It is a possible later validation site.

**7. Demos.** The open MIMIC-IV and eICU samples are too small to model. Use them to write and test your Sepsis-3 pipeline while credentialing is pending.

## Known, not confirmed

- **Paper citations:** the literature APIs returned almost nothing, so I'm citing no papers. Check the Challenge 2019 paper (Reyna et al., *Critical Care Medicine*), which the page says is the official one.
- **Contents of MIMIC-IV, eICU and AmsterdamUMCdb:** I didn't read the variable lists today. Sizes and derivation code availability are from memory.
- **Credentialing timing:** "about 1–2 weeks" is from memory.

- **Hugging Face copies of the Challenge data:** unofficial mirrors. Use PhysioNet.
- **Zenodo and OpenAIRE sepsis supplements:** these have mortality, biomarker or single-study tables, with no hourly vitals or onset times.
- **MIMIC-style datasets with only discharge codes:** ICD-coded sepsis gives no onset time.

- An open, multi-centre dataset with raw Sepsis-3 inputs and no application.
- Working literature search results this session.
- The old Amsterdam URL (amsterdammedicaldatascience.nl/amsterdamumcdb/) returned 404, so use the DOI link.

1. Today: download Challenge 2019 and run a baseline against its utility score.
2. Today: start the CITI course and the PhysioNet credentialing application. That is the slow part.
3. While you wait: build your Sepsis-3 derivation on the MIMIC-IV demo.
4. After approval: train on MIMIC-IV and validate externally on eICU. Ask the HiRID authors in parallel.

graders.name: 01-recall-physionet-2019-sepsis-challenge
graders.evidence:
The short version is that you can start on the PhysioNet/CinC 2019 Challenge data today, and the other useful datasets need one credentialing step. I'm answering from memory and didn't check live pages, so confirm current versions and processing times on each dataset's page.

## Download now, no application

**PhysioNet/Computing in Cardiology Challenge 2019, "Early Prediction of Sepsis from Clinical Data"**
- It has about 40k ICU patients from two hospital systems (training sets A and B), with hourly vitals, labs, and demographics.
- It includes a per-hour `SepsisLabel` derived from Sepsis-3 criteria. This is the only open dataset with a ready-made time-stamped onset label, so it's your week-one baseline.
- Two caveats:
  - The label is shifted about 6 hours before the Sepsis-3 onset time. That was a challenge design choice, so be careful comparing numbers with papers that don't use that shift.
  - It has only about 40 variables and no raw antibiotic or culture timestamps, so you can't re-derive onset with a different definition.
- Use the official utility score alongside AUROC and AUPRC, since prior work reports it.

The eICU demo (100 patients) is also open, but it's only useful for testing your pipeline.

## Needs credentialing (one application, several datasets)

PhysioNet credentialing is a one-time step. After it, each dataset only needs a data use agreement (DUA) signed on its page.

1. Create a PhysioNet account.
2. Complete the CITI "Data or Specimens Only Research" course, which takes a few hours.
3. Submit the credentialing form with a reference. Your supervisor is a natural choice, and they'll get an email to confirm.
4. Wait for approval. In my experience that's days to a couple of weeks, and your reference's response speed is the usual bottleneck. Start this today.
5. Sign the DUA for each dataset.

Datasets this unlocks:
- **MIMIC-IV** (single center, BIDMC) is the standard choice. The MIT-LCP `mimic-code` repo has a derived `sepsis3` table (suspected infection from antibiotics plus cultures, with SOFA ≥ 2), so you get Sepsis-3 onset times without writing the logic yourself.
- **MIMIC-III** is older. It's mostly useful for comparing against earlier papers.
- **eICU-CRD** is multi-center US (200+ hospitals), which is good for external validation. Its culture and antibiotic timing is much weaker, so Sepsis-3 onset derivation is noisier.
- **HiRID** (Bern) has high-resolution data at about 2-minute intervals. It has no official sepsis label, so you'd derive onset yourself.
- **SICdb** (Salzburg) is also on PhysioNet, I believe under the same credentialing. Check its page.

## Separate application

**AmsterdamUMCdb** is run by Amsterdam UMC. It involves a request form and a signed data sharing agreement with the institution, and it takes longer than PhysioNet. I'd treat it as a later-stage external validation set, not a week-one option.

## Tools that save time once you have access

- **ricu** (R package) harmonizes MIMIC, eICU, HiRID, and AmsterdamUMCdb into common concepts and includes a Sepsis-3 implementation.
- **YAIB** (Yet Another ICU Benchmark) has a sepsis prediction task across those datasets with preprocessing and baselines.

Both give you a consistent cohort and label definition across datasets, which matters because onset definitions differ between papers.

## Suggested plan for the week

1. **Today:** Download the Challenge data and start CITI and credentialing.
2. **Days 1–3:** Build the baseline on the Challenge data, for example gradient-boosted trees on lagged and windowed features, then a sequence model.
3. **When approved:** Sign the MIMIC-IV DUA, derive Sepsis-3 onset with `mimic-code`, and rerun your pipeline. Use eICU later for external validation.

## One compliance note

PhysioNet's DUAs generally prohibit sending the data to third-party services, including hosted LLM APIs, unless the service is covered by an approved arrangement. Check this before using any AI assistant on credentialed data, including me.

graders.name: 01-recall-italian-parkinsons-voice-speech
graders.evidence:
I found six datasets of raw PD and healthy-control audio. Four can be downloaded today, one needs a request approved, and one is gated behind institutional sign-off. I checked them on 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12. Zenodo and DataCite errored on some queries, so the search may have missed some datasets.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** actual audio files (wav/mp3), not feature tables.
- **R2 (must):** PD patients and healthy controls, labelled.
- **R3 (nice):** quick access, and a licence that allows ML training.

I assumed any language is acceptable, since you didn't specify one.

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size / contents | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | VOC-PD (Mandarin) | Open download | CC BY 4.0 | 1,551 wav files: 811 PD, 740 HC | today |
| 2 | Arabic PD Speech (Mutah Univ.) | Open download | CC BY 4.0 | 40 speakers (17 PD, 23 HC), mp3 | today |
| 3 | MDVR-KCL (London, smartphone) | Open download | CC BY 4.0 | early and advanced PD plus HC | today |
| 4 | Italian Parkinson's Voice and Speech | Free IEEE DataPort account | CC BY (as stated on the page) | wav, ~565 MB | today |
| 5 | NeuroVoz (Castilian Spanish) | Request access, accept a data agreement; I'd guess days to weeks | CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 | multi-task corpus with controls | today |
| 6 | Bridge2AI-Voice | Raw audio via Synapse, needs institutional sign-off; likely weeks to months | Registered Access licence | large, multi-condition; 263 controls | today |

## Details
- **VOC-PD:** https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21775027. It has five task folders: numbers, phrases, sentences, vowels and monophthongs. Download directly from Zenodo. It was published in August 2026, so no papers use it yet. I didn't check how the diagnoses were confirmed.
- **Arabic PD:** https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22036480. It has sustained vowels, a read passage and spontaneous speech. There are only 40 subjects, so split by speaker to avoid leakage. The mp3 format is lossy.
- **MDVR-KCL:** https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.2867215. I didn't confirm exact subject counts from the page text. A 2021 arXiv comparison paper used it alongside the Italian corpus (https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2111.10207).
- **Italian:** https://ieee-dataport.org/open-access/italian-parkinsons-voice-and-speech. The page says "Open Access dataset files are accessible to all logged in users", but it also mentions an IEEE DataPort Subscription. Check what the free account actually gives you. HuggingFace copies exist (e.g. `birgermoell/Italian_Parkinsons_Voice_and_Speech`); they are third-party mirrors, so use the IEEE original. A 2024 *Journal of Voice* paper on audio spectrogram transformers (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jvoice.2024.11.008) came up for this corpus.
- **NeuroVoz:** https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13647600. Zenodo says "The record is publicly accessible, but files are restricted" and that you accept a Data Agreement Usage through request access. The non-commercial, no-derivatives licence may limit sharing models or derived features, so read the agreement. An Interspeech 2025 paper (https://doi.org/10.21437/interspeech.2025-801) used it with pre-trained audio embeddings.
- **Bridge2AI-Voice:** https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/4.0.0/. PhysioNet says raw audio "requires institutional sign off" and goes through Synapse, with requests to DACO@b2ai-voice.org. I didn't check how many PD participants it has. It's a weaker fit than the others.

## Known, not confirmed
These are from memory. I didn't confirm them today.
- **PC-GITA** (Colombian Spanish, GITA group, Univ. of Antioquia): widely used, with sustained vowels, DDK and sentences. As I recall, you request it from the authors and sign a license agreement. It isn't openly downloadable.
- **Czech PD corpora (Rusz et al.):** I recall these as available only on request from the authors.
- **mPower (Sage Bionetworks, Synapse):** voice recordings from a smartphone study of PD patients and controls. As I recall, you register on Synapse and pass a qualification step. I tried the portal (https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn4993293), but the page loads by JavaScript and returned no text. Controls there are self-reported and not clinically confirmed, which weakens labels.

## Not recommended, and why
- **Zenodo 10406860 (plosive consonants):** extracted features only, no audio.
- **Two figshare records** (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.32588973.v2 and https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.33212514.v1): described as extracted acoustic features and voice measurements. I couldn't open the pages because of a bot challenge, so they may contain audio, but I doubt it.
- **Synthetic PD voice records on Zenodo:** synthetic data, not real patients.
- **UCI/Oxford PD tables:** these are feature tables, which you ruled out (from memory).

## What I could not find
I found no large English-language PD corpus that you can simply download. Pooling the open sets above gives you four languages, which suits cross-corpus work but adds language and recording-device confounds.

## Next step
Start with VOC-PD, Arabic, MDVR-KCL and Italian today. Submit the NeuroVoz request now, since it's the slow one. Train and test by speaker, and hold out an entire corpus to test generalisation. Two of these sets are small, so a single-corpus score will look better than it should.

- **Bridge2AI-Voice:** https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/4.0.0/. PhysioNet says raw audio "requires institutional sign off" and goes through Synapse, with requests to DACO@b2ai-voice.org. I didn't check how many PD participants it has. It's a weaker fit than the others.

## Known, not confirmed

- **PC-GITA** (Colombian Spanish, GITA group, Univ. of Antioquia): widely used, with sustained vowels, DDK and sentences. As I recall, you request it from the authors and sign a license agreement. It isn't openly downloadable.
- **Czech PD corpora (Rusz et al.):** I recall these as available only on request from the authors.

- **UCI/Oxford PD tables:** these are feature tables, which you ruled out (from memory).

graders.name: 01-recall-italian-parkinsons-voice-speech
graders.evidence:
I found three PD-vs-control speech datasets with real audio that you can download today. A fourth, IPVS (Italian Parkinson's Voice and Speech), needs a free login. Two more are well known but gated. I did not build the interactive shortlist page, so everything is in this message.

I searched Zenodo, DataCite, OpenAIRE, PhysioNet, Hugging Face and the literature. I checked records and access flags on 2026-11-11, and the checks were partial. Figshare and IEEE sites blocked automated page reads, and the Zenodo search failed on one query. Treat the list as good but not exhaustive.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** raw audio, not feature tables.
- **R2 (must):** PD and healthy-control labels.
- **R3 (nice):** several speakers and several tasks (vowels, reading, spontaneous speech), so you can split by speaker.
- **R4 (nice):** open or fast access, and a licence that allows research use.

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **MDVR-KCL** (UK, phone-recorded) | Direct download from Zenodo | CC-BY-4.0 | 606 MB zip | Audio, PD and HC | Today |
| 2 | **VOC-PD** (Mandarin) | Direct download from Zenodo | CC-BY-4.0 | 1,551 .wav files (811 PD, 740 HC) | Audio, PD and HC, 5 tasks | Today (record only, files not opened) |
| 3 | **Arabic PD Speech Dataset** | Direct download from Zenodo | CC-BY-4.0 | 39 MB, 17 PD and 23 HC | Audio, PD and HC, 3 task types | Today (record only) |
| 4 | **Italian Parkinson's Voice and Speech (IPVS)** | Free IEEE DataPort login (my reading of the page, below) | Not stated on the page I could read | ~565 MB | Audio, PD and HC | Today (page), contents from memory |
| 5 | **Bridge2AI-Voice** | Registered access for features; raw audio needs institutional sign-off and a committee decision | Custom "Registered Access" licence | 48,226 recordings, 263 control participants | Mixed-condition cohort with a PD diagnosis table | Today |
| 6 | **PC-GITA** (Colombian Spanish) | Agreement with the owning group | Unknown | 50 PD and 50 HC | Audio, PD and HC | From memory |

## Details

**1. MDVR-KCL.** https://zenodo.org/records/2867216 (the DOI 10.5281/zenodo.2867215 also resolves).
- **What it is:** recordings made on a mobile phone at King's College London Hospital in September 2017. Zenodo's description says it covers early and advanced PD patients and healthy controls.
- **Access:** open on Zenodo, one zip file, no account needed.
- **Licence:** CC-BY-4.0, so attribution is the only requirement.
- **From memory (not confirmed today):** about 37 speakers, with reading and spontaneous tasks. The set is small, so split by speaker and be careful about overfitting.
- **Use in papers:** one 2021 arXiv comparison paper used it together with IPVS (https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2111.10207).
- **Hugging Face copy:** the Hugging Face copy `saeedzou/kcl-parkinson-voice-dataset` is a re-upload. Use Zenodo.

**2. VOC-PD.** https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21775027
- **What it is:** Mandarin audio in .wav format, in 5 task folders (numbers, phrases, sentences, vowels and one more).
- **Why it fits:** it is the largest clean-labelled open audio set I found, and the PD and HC counts are well balanced.
- **Caveats:** it is brand new (October 2026) and has no citations yet. The record doesn't give a speaker count, so check that recordings can be grouped by speaker before you split train and test.
- **Access and licence:** open on Zenodo under CC-BY-4.0.

**3. Arabic PD Speech Dataset.** https://zenodo.org/records/22036480
- **What it is:** 40 speakers. Tasks are sustained /a/, /i/ and /u/, a read passage and spontaneous speech.
- **Caveat:** the small speaker count makes it better for external validation than for training.
- **Access and licence:** open on Zenodo under CC-BY-4.0 (version 1.0.0, August 2026).

**4. IPVS.** https://www.ieee-dataport.org/open-access/italian-parkinsons-voice-and-speech (DOI 10.21227/aw6b-tg17)
- **Access:** the page says "LOGIN TO ACCESS DATASET FILES", and another passage mentions an IEEE DataPort subscription. I could not fully read the page, so confirm whether a free account is enough before planning around it.
- **Licence:** not stated on the page I could read. Check it on DataPort.
- **From memory:** about 65 speakers. The healthy controls include young adults as well as elderly ones, which creates an age confound you should control for.
- **Mirrors:** several Hugging Face copies exist (for example `birgermoell/Italian_Parkinsons_Voice_and_Speech`, ungated, with a 1.66k-row audio table). They are third-party re-uploads, and the CC-BY-4.0 tag was set by the uploader. For citations and licence certainty, use DataPort.
- **Use in papers:** a 2024 Journal of Voice paper on audio spectrogram transformers (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jvoice.2024.11.008) is in the literature results, but I did not confirm which dataset it used.

**5. Bridge2AI-Voice.** https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/4.0.0/
- **What it is:** a large, multi-condition voice collection with a Parkinson's diagnosis table (`parkinsons_disease.tsv`) and 263 controls.
- **Access, quoted from the page:** "Raw Audio Data Access for Bridge2AI Voice Adult Cohort is via Synapse" and "Accessing raw audio is a more involved process and requires institutional sign-off." Contact: DACO@b2ai-voice.org.
- **What I did not get:** the number of PD participants, and whether the PhysioNet release includes audio or only derived features.
- **Timeline:** plan on weeks, not days.

**6. PC-GITA.** From memory, not confirmed today.
- **What it is:** Colombian Spanish from the GITA group at Universidad de Antioquia, with about 50 PD and 50 HC speakers. A 2026 conference paper in the literature results uses it (https://doi.org/10.1109/icsadl67539.2026.11451863).
- **Access (my recollection):** a data-use agreement with the owning group. I couldn't open the IEEE page to confirm, so email the group.

## Known, not confirmed
- **Neurovoz** (Castilian Spanish PD corpus). I recall it as audio, with access by request to the authors (possibly via Zenodo). I did not verify this. Search "Neurovoz" and read the access statement.
- **Czech PD speech** (Rusz and colleagues). I recall access by request to the authors. Unverified, and "on request" is not an open dataset.
- **Figshare "Parkinson-Disease-voice-Dataset"** (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.32588973.v2). It is open under CC-BY-4.0 and about 697 MB. But the description talks about "acoustic speech features", so it may be features only. The landing page was blocked, so open it and check whether it contains .wav files.
- **University of Rochester dataset** (https://doi.org/10.60593/ur.d.29410703.v2). The title says "Parkinson's Disease Screening", and it carries a CC-BY-4.0 licence. The page was blocked and the registry gave no access flag, so check the contents yourself.

## Not recommended
- **UCI Parkinson's voice sets** (Little et al. and the Sakar multi-type set). I recall these as precomputed measures, which is what you ruled out. This is from memory.
- **Mendeley "voice features from diadochokinesis test"** (https://doi.org/10.17632/zdp72s54cd.1). The title says features, and I didn't open it.
- **Figshare "Dataset for Parkinson Disease"** (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.33212514.v1). "Biomedical voice measurements" sounds like a feature table, and I didn't open it.
- **"Synthetic Voice Dataset for Parkinson's…"** (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17753641). It is synthetic, and probably not audio.
- **PhysioNet PADS** (smartwatch motion data) and **Hugging Face `Parkinson_Speech` variants** (`BenchmarkDatasets`, `TabBioMed`). They don't fit: PADS is motion data, and the Hugging Face ones look like tabular copies of the UCI data.

## What I could not find
- A large, multi-site open corpus with hundreds of PD speakers and matched controls. The open sets are all small to medium (tens of speakers, or a few thousand clips).
- I did not search the Synapse portal directly (mPower, which I recall as app-collected voice with PD and control labels). From memory, it needs a free account plus an approved qualified-researcher application. Check it if you need scale.

## Next step
1. **Today:** download MDVR-KCL, VOC-PD and the Arabic set from Zenodo. They use three languages and three recording setups, which suits cross-corpus testing.
2. **This week:** create an IEEE DataPort account for IPVS, and email the PC-GITA and Neurovoz groups.
3. **For the model:** split by speaker, not by clip, because every dataset here has multiple clips per person. Train on one corpus and test on another to see whether your detector learns PD or just the recording setup.

If you want the interactive shortlist page, I can build it.

I found three PD-vs-control speech datasets with real audio that you can download today. A fourth, IPVS (Italian Parkinson's Voice and Speech), needs a free login. Two more are well known but gated. I did not build the interactive shortlist page, so everything is in this message.

I searched Zenodo, DataCite, OpenAIRE, PhysioNet, Hugging Face and the literature. I checked records and access flags on 2026-11-11, and the checks were partial. Figshare and IEEE sites blocked automated page reads, and the Zenodo search failed on one query. Treat the list as good but not exhaustive.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** raw audio, not feature tables.
- **R2 (must):** PD and healthy-control labels.
- **R3 (nice):** several speakers and several tasks (vowels, reading, spontaneous speech), so you can split by speaker.
- **R4 (nice):** open or fast access, and a licence that allows research use.

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **MDVR-KCL** (UK, phone-recorded) | Direct download from Zenodo | CC-BY-4.0 | 606 MB zip | Audio, PD and HC | Today |
| 2 | **VOC-PD** (Mandarin) | Direct download from Zenodo | CC-BY-4.0 | 1,551 .wav files (811 PD, 740 HC) | Audio, PD and HC, 5 tasks | Today (record only, files not opened) |
| 3 | **Arabic PD Speech Dataset** | Direct download from Zenodo | CC-BY-4.0 | 39 MB, 17 PD and 23 HC | Audio, PD and HC, 3 task types | Today (record only) |
| 4 | **Italian Parkinson's Voice and Speech (IPVS)** | Free IEEE DataPort login (my reading of the page, below) | Not stated on the page I could read | ~565 MB | Audio, PD and HC | Today (page), contents from memory |
| 5 | **Bridge2AI-Voice** | Registered access for features; raw audio needs institutional sign-off and a committee decision | Custom "Registered Access" licence | 48,226 recordings, 263 control participants | Mixed-condition cohort with a PD diagnosis table | Today |
| 6 | **PC-GITA** (Colombian Spanish) | Agreement with the owning group | Unknown | 50 PD and 50 HC | Audio, PD and HC | From memory |

## Details

**1. MDVR-KCL.** https://zenodo.org/records/2867216 (the DOI 10.5281/zenodo.2867215 also resolves).
- **What it is:** recordings made on a mobile phone at King's College London Hospital in September 2017. Zenodo's description says it covers early and advanced PD patients and healthy controls.
- **Access:** open on Zenodo, one zip file, no account needed.
- **Licence:** CC-BY-4.0, so attribution is the only requirement.
- **From memory (not confirmed today):** about 37 speakers, with reading and spontaneous tasks. The set is small, so split by speaker and be careful about overfitting.
- **Use in papers:** one 2021 arXiv comparison paper used it together with IPVS (https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2111.10207).
- **Hugging Face copy:** the Hugging Face copy `saeedzou/kcl-parkinson-voice-dataset` is a re-upload. Use Zenodo.

**2. VOC-PD.** https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21775027
- **What it is:** Mandarin audio in .wav format, in 5 task folders (numbers, phrases, sentences, vowels and one more).
- **Why it fits:** it is the largest clean-labelled open audio set I found, and the PD and HC counts are well balanced.
- **Caveats:** it is brand new (October 2026) and has no citations yet. The record doesn't give a speaker count, so check that recordings can be grouped by speaker before you split train and test.
- **Access and licence:** open on Zenodo under CC-BY-4.0.

**3. Arabic PD Speech Dataset.** https://zenodo.org/records/22036480
- **What it is:** 40 speakers. Tasks are sustained /a/, /i/ and /u/, a read passage and spontaneous speech.
- **Caveat:** the small speaker count makes it better for external validation than for training.
- **Access and licence:** open on Zenodo under CC-BY-4.0 (version 1.0.0, August 2026).

**4. IPVS.** https://www.ieee-dataport.org/open-access/italian-parkinsons-voice-and-speech (DOI 10.21227/aw6b-tg17)
- **Access:** the page says "LOGIN TO ACCESS DATASET FILES", and another passage mentions an IEEE DataPort subscription. I could not fully read the page, so confirm whether a free account is enough before planning around it.
- **Licence:** not stated on the page I could read. Check it on DataPort.
- **From memory:** about 65 speakers. The healthy controls include young adults as well as elderly ones, which creates an age confound you should control for.
- **Mirrors:** several Hugging Face copies exist (for example `birgermoell/Italian_Parkinsons_Voice_and_Speech`, ungated, with a 1.66k-row audio table). They are third-party re-uploads, and the CC-BY-4.0 tag was set by the uploader. For citations and licence certainty, use DataPort.
- **Use in papers:** a 2024 Journal of Voice paper on audio spectrogram transformers (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jvoice.2024.11.008) is in the literature results, but I did not confirm which dataset it used.

**5. Bridge2AI-Voice.** https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/4.0.0/
- **What it is:** a large, multi-condition voice collection with a Parkinson's diagnosis table (`parkinsons_disease.tsv`) and 263 controls.
- **Access, quoted from the page:** "Raw Audio Data Access for Bridge2AI Voice Adult Cohort is via Synapse" and "Accessing raw audio is a more involved process and requires institutional sign-off." Contact: DACO@b2ai-voice.org.
- **What I did not get:** the number of PD participants, and whether the PhysioNet release includes audio or only derived features.
- **Timeline:** plan on weeks, not days.

**6. PC-GITA.** From memory, not confirmed today.
- **What it is:** Colombian Spanish from the GITA group at Universidad de Antioquia, with about 50 PD and 50 HC speakers. A 2026 conference paper in the literature results uses it (https://doi.org/10.1109/icsadl67539.2026.11451863).
- **Access (my recollection):** a data-use agreement with the owning group. I couldn't open the IEEE page to confirm, so email the group.

## Known, not confirmed
- **Neurovoz** (Castilian Spanish PD corpus). I recall it as audio, with access by request to the authors (possibly via Zenodo). I did not verify this. Search "Neurovoz" and read the access statement.
- **Czech PD speech** (Rusz and colleagues). I recall access by request to the authors. Unverified, and "on request" is not an open dataset.
- **Figshare "Parkinson-Disease-voice-Dataset"** (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.32588973.v2). It is open under CC-BY-4.0 and about 697 MB. But the description talks about "acoustic speech features", so it may be features only. The landing page was blocked, so open it and check whether it contains .wav files.
- **University of Rochester dataset** (https://doi.org/10.60593/ur.d.29410703.v2). The title says "Parkinson's Disease Screening", and it carries a CC-BY-4.0 licence. The page was blocked and the registry gave no access flag, so check the contents yourself.

## Not recommended
- **UCI Parkinson's voice sets** (Little et al. and the Sakar multi-type set). I recall these as precomputed measures, which is what you ruled out. This is from memory.
- **Mendeley "voice features from diadochokinesis test"** (https://doi.org/10.17632/zdp72s54cd.1). The title says features, and I didn't open it.
- **Figshare "Dataset for Parkinson Disease"** (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.33212514.v1). "Biomedical voice measurements" sounds like a feature table, and I didn't open it.
- **"Synthetic Voice Dataset for Parkinson's…"** (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17753641). It is synthetic, and probably not audio.
- **PhysioNet PADS** (smartwatch motion data) and **Hugging Face `Parkinson_Speech` variants** (`BenchmarkDatasets`, `TabBioMed`). They don't fit: PADS is motion data, and the Hugging Face ones look like tabular copies of the UCI data.

## What I could not find
- A large, multi-site open corpus with hundreds of PD speakers and matched controls. The open sets are all small to medium (tens of speakers, or a few thousand clips).
- I did not search the Synapse portal directly (mPower, which I recall as app-collected voice with PD and control labels). From memory, it needs a free account plus an approved qualified-researcher application. Check it if you need scale.

## Next step
1. **Today:** download MDVR-KCL, VOC-PD and the Arabic set from Zenodo. They use three languages and three recording setups, which suits cross-corpus testing.
2. **This week:** create an IEEE DataPort account for IPVS, and email the PC-GITA and Neurovoz groups.
3. **For the model:** split by speaker, not by clip, because every dataset here has multiple clips per person. Train on one corpus and test on another to see whether your detector learns PD or just the recording setup.

If you want the interactive shortlist page, I can build it.

graders.name: 01-recall-italian-parkinsons-voice-speech
graders.evidence:
I haven't checked any of these links or access terms live, so confirm them on each landing page. Everything below is from memory.

## Open download (audio included)

| Dataset | Contents | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **Italian Parkinson's Voice and Speech** (Dimauro & Girardi, Bari) | About 65 speakers (roughly 28 PD and 37 HC). It has sustained vowels, words and phrases, in about 830 recordings. | Hosted on IEEE DataPort. Make a free account and download. It's CC-BY, and there are Kaggle mirrors. |
| **MDVR-KCL** (King's College London mobile voice recordings) | About 37 speakers (16 PD and 21 HC). It has smartphone recordings of reading and spontaneous speech. | Zenodo, open, CC-BY. Search for "MDVR-KCL". |

## Registration or a request required

| Dataset | Contents | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **mPower** (Sage Bionetworks) | Thousands of smartphone participants, each doing a 10-second "aaah". PD status is self-reported. It's the largest set by far. | On Synapse. Make an account, complete the qualified-researcher/data-use steps, and accept the conditions. Approval can take a while. |
| **PC-GITA** (Universidad de Antioquia, Colombian Spanish) | 50 PD and 50 HC, age- and sex-balanced. It has vowels, DDK tasks, sentences and a monologue. | Not a public download. Email the GITA group and sign a license, usually academic-only. |
| **Neurovoz** (Castilian Spanish) | About 100+ speakers (PD and HC), with several speech tasks. | Distributed on request, with a data agreement. Check the Zenodo and paper listing for the current process. |

graders.name: 01-recall-italian-parkinsons-voice-speech
graders.evidence:
I'm working from memory and haven't checked the current pages, so confirm access terms and sizes at the source before you build on any of this.

## Openly downloadable

| Dataset | Contents | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **MDVR-KCL** (King's College London, Jaeger et al. 2019) | About 37 speakers (about 21 PD, 16 HC). Smartphone recordings of reading and spontaneous speech. | Zenodo, open download, CC-BY. Search "Mobile Device Voice Recordings at King's College London". |
| **Italian Parkinson's Voice and Speech** (Dimauro & Girardi) | About 65 speakers (28 PD, 37 HC). Sustained vowels, words, and sentences as WAV. | IEEE DataPort. You need a free account, and I believe it's open access. |
| **Neurovoz** (Castilian Spanish, Mendes-Laureano et al., 2024) | About 100 speakers, PD and HC. Vowels, DDK, sentences, and free speech. | I believe it's on Zenodo, possibly with a request step. Check the paper's data-availability statement. |

## Registration and approval required

- **mPower** (Sage Bionetworks, Synapse): This is the largest set by far, with thousands of participants. The recordings are 10-second "aaah" phonations from smartphones, in m4a.
  - **Access:** Create a Synapse account, complete the Certified User process, and submit a data access request with a statement of intended use.
  - **Caveat:** Many diagnosis labels are self-reported, and the audio quality varies a lot.

## Available only by request to the authors

- **PC-GITA** (Colombian Spanish, Orozco-Arroyave et al.): 50 PD and 50 HC, with a rich task set. It's the most-used benchmark in the literature. Contact the GITA group at Universidad de Antioquia, who usually require a data-use agreement.
- **Czech and German PD corpora** (Rusz, Prague, and Erlangen groups): These are also by request. Email the corresponding authors of the papers.

## Datasets to avoid

These come up in searches but don't contain audio:
- **UCI Oxford Parkinson's (Little)**, **UCI Parkinson's Telemonitoring**, and most **Kaggle "Parkinson's voice" sets** are precomputed features only.
- **UCI Sakar multiple-sound-types set** is mostly features, so check whether the raw WAVs are included before relying on it.
- **Bridge2AI-Voice** (PhysioNet) includes PD, but as far as I know the public release has derived features rather than raw audio. Check the current release notes.

## Caveats for deep learning

- **Size:** The open sets are small, with dozens of speakers each. Split by speaker, never by clip, or you'll get inflated accuracy from speaker leakage.
- **Recording confounds:** If PD and HC were recorded with different devices or rooms, a model can learn the channel instead of the disease. Check this per dataset, especially for mPower and MDVR-KCL.
- **Pooling:** Combining datasets helps generalization, but language and task differ across them. Hold out a whole dataset as a test set if you can.
- **Labels:** Check how each dataset defines and verifies diagnosis. Also check medication state (on or off) and severity scores (UPDRS, H&Y) where they're provided.
